facts.fact: As part of the SCART rollout launched in Hoima city on 22 September 2026, the Ministry of Local Government provided a laptop and a router to support data entry and use of the web-based system in Hoima East and West divisions, for official business only, on its financial management specialist's word.
facts.system: laptop and router provided with SCART

facts.fact: SCART, a web-based financial management system of the Ministry of Local Government for accounting, budgeting and financial reporting in lower local governments and service delivery units, was launched on 22 September 2026 for use by Hoima East and West divisions, which had until then worked manually, on their principal treasurers' word.
facts.system: Simplified Computerised Accounting and Reporting Tool (SCART)

facts.fact: The web-based SCART had been rolled out in 66 units by 22 September 2026, 25 of them lower local governments and 41 health units and schools, on the Ministry of Local Government permanent secretary's word; no total of lower local governments is given, and the document does not say how units other than Hoima's divisions are connected.
facts.system: Simplified Computerised Accounting and Reporting Tool (SCART)

facts.fact: The Ministry of Local Government launched SCART in Hoima city's two divisions on 22 September 2026, supplying a laptop and router for its use.
facts.system: Simplified Computerised Accounting and Reporting Tool (SCART)

facts.fact: SCART is rolled out by the Ministry of Local Government, which supplied the laptop and router and trained its staff, and was developed with the ministries of Education and Sports, Finance and Health, as stated at the Hoima launch of 22 September 2026.
facts.system: Simplified Computerised Accounting and Reporting Tool (SCART)

facts.fact: The report of the SCART launch in Hoima on 22 September 2026 names no budget or funder for the tool or the laptop and router.
facts.system: Simplified Computerised Accounting and Reporting Tool (SCART)
